name: Unmet goals pursued within their budget
purpose: An unmet goal is pursued with the untried reads within its budget, never writes, says once that the rest is still being worked on when it is long, and ends in a met goal or an honest account of what was tried and what is missing.
record: Fifteen scripted cases (evaluation/critical_thinking/build_cases.py) with a stub check and a stub attempt: met on the first pass with no loop, met after one or two replans, unmet and unrecoverable (the best response plus what was tried and what is missing), a write that is never offered or accepted, the replan cap and the wall cap respected, and a long job announced exactly once, inline or as the plan for a background follow-up. A private set of badly handled inputs can add one case per input when the environment names it (HUB_POORLY_ANSWERED_INPUTS); none of it is kept in this repository. One number: the share of cases whose summary equals the expected one. Later stages (acceptance cases on a live consumer) rise in fidelity and keep this number.
disadvantages: The first stage uses stubs for the check and the attempt, so it shows the decisions hold, not that a real model finds the missing part.
cascading_conditionals: idea [kind=idea | scale=esoi/idea-rating-scale.md | min-pass-rate=0.75 | when=a new alternative is described: rate its description on the five questions of the scale before it is built] > offline [real=no | gate=all-pass | when=requests with known answers through a fake model] > one [sample=sample:1 | real=yes | gate=all-pass | when=a single real case runs end to end and is hand-read] > staged [sample=sample | real=yes | gate=competitive | max-age-days=90 | when=a call budget is set and the spend is approved] > whole [sample=full | real=yes | max-age-days=90 | when=the staged sample did not decide]
